notes:
I couldn't get any source material for Jeremiah 44, so I haven't written any notes yet.

I tried to fetch six pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Bible Hub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. My code crashed before it printed anything, so I never saw what those pages contain. The tool then hit its limit for this turn, which blocked a retry and the searches I'd planned for the "Queen of Heaven" and the other-views sources. Your rule is to report only what the pages actually say, so I've left the notes blank rather than fill them in from memory.

If you ask again, I'll start with these pages:

- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-44/, biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jeremiah/44.htm, …/pulpit/jeremiah/44.htm, …/gill/jeremiah/44.htm, and the Jeremiah 44 commentary on preceptaustin.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Jeremiah 44 at netbible.org, and bibleodyssey.org on the Queen of Heaven.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** catholic.com and newadvent.org on the Queen of Heaven (vv. 17–19, 25), where Catholic writers respond to the Protestant claim that this passage bears on Marian titles.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** gotquestions.org, desiringgod.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes) and Spurgeon's sermons on the people's argument that idolatry made them prosper (vv. 17–18) and on God's oath in vv. 26–27. I'd also check whether any site ties that "we had plenty" argument to prosperity teaching.

I'll then write the notes verse by verse with a URL for every point, and leave out anything the pages don't cover.
